## Theme: `theme_microdrive()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_microdrive()`, built from IBM and Hitachi Microdrive cards on a tan desk: a black frame, a red title, IBM blue, red, navy, and Hitachi sky blue marks, and a Times New Roman title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1999)
microdrive_photos <- tibble(
  photo_id = 1:300,
  size_mb = round(rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(0.75), sdlog = 0.8), 2)
)
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```

::::

## Description

Violin plots show data distribution and probability density. They are like box plots but have a rotated kernel density plot on each side. We can use them to compare data distribution across categories.

::: {.column-margin}

The violin plot is essentially a mirrored density plot, in which a smoothed distribution is plotted symmetrically across the `x` or `y` axis, creating a Rorschach-like inkblot area for the distribution:

![source: Rorschach test, Wikipedia](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/70/Rorschach_blot_01.jpg){fig-align="right" width="80%"}
:::

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}
Install packages.
:::


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}
In 1999, IBM's 340MB Microdrive squeezed a tiny spinning hard disk into a CompactFlash Type II card, giving digital camera owners room for hundreds of photos. The photo files varied a lot in size: most JPEGs came in under a megabyte, but detailed scenes and high quality settings produced a few much larger files. We'll simulate 300 photo files with `rlnorm()`, rounding each size to the nearest hundredth of a megabyte. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 300 file sizes every time you run the code below.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1999)
microdrive_photos <- tibble(
  photo_id = 1:300,
  size_mb = round(rlnorm(n = 300, meanlog = log(0.75), sdlog = 0.8), 2)
)
glimpse(microdrive_photos)
```
:::

## Distribution

File sizes are a classic example of data that can't go below zero but can stretch a long way above it. That gives the violin a wide base and a long, thin neck. The trick to understanding this shape is the logarithm: on a log scale, these file sizes turn into the familiar bell curve from @sec-histograms. Below we'll move from the file sizes, to a picture, to the formula.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first ten photos.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
head(microdrive_photos$size_mb, 10)
```
:::

Most of these are under 1.5 MB, but three are near or above 2 MB. A few large files like these pull the mean well above the median. Taking the log of each file size shrinks the gap.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
microdrive_photos |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(size_mb), 
    median = median(size_mb),
    mean_log = mean(log(size_mb)),
    median_log = median(log(size_mb)))
```
:::

On the megabyte scale, the mean is about `r round(mean(microdrive_photos$size_mb) - median(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB higher than the median. On the log scale, the mean and median are almost identical, which is what we'd expect from a symmetric distribution.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

A bar model splits the photos at 0.75 MB (we'll see why in a moment). The two parts are close to equal, so 0.75 MB sits near the middle of the file sizes.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_bar_model_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.45
microdrive_photos |> 
  mutate(range = factor(if_else(size_mb < 0.75, "under 0.75 MB", "0.75 MB or more"),
    levels = c("under 0.75 MB", "0.75 MB or more"))) |> 
  count(range) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = "300 photos", fill = range)) + 
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = n), color = "white", 
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE)) + 
  labs(x = "Number of photos", y = NULL, fill = "File size")
```
:::

Below are two violins of the same 300 file sizes. The first uses megabytes, so most of the area is squashed near the bottom and the neck stretches up past 5 MB. The second puts the `y` axis on a log scale with `scale_y_log10()`, which turns the same file sizes into a symmetric shape centered near 0.75 MB.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(data = microdrive_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  labs(title = "Megabyte scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB)")

ggplot(data = microdrive_photos, aes(x = "", y = size_mb)) + 
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(title = "Log scale", x = NULL, y = "File size (MB, log scale)")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

The `rlnorm()` call that created the data draws from a [log normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log-normal_distribution). A file size is log normal when its logarithm is normal:

$$
\log(X) \sim \text{Normal}(\mu = \log(0.75), \sigma = 0.8)
$$

The two parameters describe the log scale, not the megabyte scale. Back on the megabyte scale, the median is $e^{\mu} = 0.75$ MB, which is why the bar model split the photos at 0.75 MB. The mean is larger, $e^{\mu + \sigma^2 / 2} = 0.75 \times e^{0.32} \approx 1.03$ MB, because the long right tail pulls it up. The bigger $\sigma$ gets, the longer the violin's neck and the further the mean drifts from the median.

Our simulated photos come close: the median is `r round(median(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB and the mean is `r round(mean(microdrive_photos$size_mb), 2)` MB.


## Grammar 

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95rem;"}

Create labels with `labs()`

Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Place an empty string (`""`) in the `x` argument

Map an empty string (`""`) to the `x` and `size_mb` to the `y`

Add `geom_violin()`

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_violin
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true 
#| warning: false
#| message: false
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_violin
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_violin <- labs(
  title = "IBM Microdrive photo file sizes",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  subtitle = "300 photos saved to a 340MB card in 1999",
  x = "",
  y = "File size (MB)")
ggp2_violin <- ggplot(data = microdrive_photos,
       aes(x = '', 
           y = size_mb)) +
       geom_violin() 
ggp2_violin + 
  labs_violin
```
